item.title: On the Connected Components of Structure Graphs of Associative Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.07521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article studies the notion of the structure graph of an associative ring with unity. It is known that the structural graph of a ring with $n$ elements has at least $n$ connected components. The article investigates when this lower bound is attained. A hypothesis is stated that the only rings of order $n$ having exactly $n$ connected components are the rings $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_7$, $GF(4)$, and their direct sums. The hypothesis is proved for all rings except residue rings modulo a prime of the form $7+12k$, $k\geq181$, and Galois fields of characteristic~2 with extension degree $\geq17$.
item.dc:creator: Andrey M. Chernev, Nikolay A. Chernev

item.title: Local and 2-Local Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Zinbiel Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.07863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study local and $2$-local derivations of finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebras. Over any field of characteristic zero, every Zinbiel algebra $A$ with $A^2 \neq 0$ and $\dim A \leq 4$ admits a proper local derivation. The proof uses a filtration argument. We exhibit two five-dimensional Zinbiel algebras with nonzero multiplication whose derivations are all central. Every local derivation on either algebra is therefore a derivation, so the minimum dimension for local rigidity with nonzero multiplication is five. Annihilator-valued interpolation gives a general construction of proper local derivations. When $A^3 = 0$, the multiplication tensor describes all derivations and local derivations. For a finite-dimensional nilpotent algebra $A$ over any field, we show that every $2$-local derivation is a derivation if and only if $\dim(A/A^2) \leq 1$. The proof combines the annihilator interpolation of Sh. Ayupov, K. Kudaybergenov and B. Omirov with a one-generator argument. When all derivations are central, every $2$-local derivation is obtained by composing a homogeneous map $A/A^2 \to \text{Ann}(A)$ with the quotient map, and every such composition is a $2$-local derivation. The five-dimensional examples extend to locally rigid Zinbiel algebras with nonlinear $2$-local derivations in every dimension at least five. We also show that derivations given by left multiplication form a Lie ideal of nilpotency class at most two and give sufficient conditions for the existence of left outer derivations. This ideal is zero in our locally rigid examples.
item.dc:creator: Arislanbay Abdireymov, Aloberdi Sattarov, Bakhtiyor Yusupov

item.title: Linear bounds and sharp exponential growth for commuting matrix algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.08135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For any $m$ pairwise commuting matrices $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{m}\subset \M_n(\F)$, we prove $\dim_\F \F[A_1,\cdots, A_m]\leq (2^m-1)(n-1)+1$, answering Bergman's question on the existence of a linear bound for a fixed number $m$.
item.dc:creator: Jiamei Li, Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Yilin Zeng

item.title: Simple Modules over Leavitt Path Algebras Generated by Indicator Functions on Paths
item.description: arXiv:2611.08344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let E be an arbitrary graph, K a field, and D the set of boundary paths of E consisting of both infinite paths and finite paths ending at singular vertices. The space KD of K-valued functions on D is a right module over the Leavitt path algebra LK(E). For a non- empty set S ? D that is strongly connected and closed under adding and deleting initial segments, we study the submodule N_S = 1_S.LK(E) generated by the indicator function of S. Let S_0 be the set of vertices lying on the paths in S. We show that N_S is simple if and only if S contains no breaking vertex of the hereditary saturated set H = E0 nS0. In particular, when S contains only infinite paths or when E is a row- finite graph, NS is a simple module. Up to isomorphism, the simple module NS depends only on S_0. When S is an infinite set of paths, the simple module NS is neither graded nor projective. The left module LK(E)1_S, obtained by twisting the action through the involution of LK(E), is simple exactly when NS is, and, when S is infinite, it is not isomorphic to any of the Chen simple modules. For the rose graph R_n with n ? 2 petals, we show that LK(R_n)1_S is isomorphic to one of the twisted Chen modules constructed by Nam, Srivastava and Vien, and to none of the other simple modules in their list. Moreover, when S is not a single vertex, the simple module NS is finitely presented if and only if only finitely many edges of E have both source and range in S_0; in particular, every simple module N_S is finitely presented when E is a finite graph. Finally, we determine when the analogous module generated by an indicator function over the Cohn path algebra CK(E) is simple. 1.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pacheco, Kulumani M. Rangaswamy

item.title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
item.description: arXiv:2611.07549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $\Lambda$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. An indecomposable $\Lambda$-module can split after extending $K$. The number of its distinct geometric indecomposable summands is the degree of its residue endomorphism field $\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)/\operatorname{rad}\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)$. We use the positive roots and cyclic automorphism of the unfolded quiver to determine the number of isomorphism classes at every nonzero rank and residue degree $e\ge1$: it is zero, an explicitly computable finite number, or $|K|$. For every invariant imaginary root of the unfolding, including at nonprimitive ranks, we construct a smooth invariant family of absolutely indecomposable representations whose rational quotient by the change-of-bases group has dimension $1-q_d(\beta)$. We characterize ranks admitting absolutely Schur representations by the Schur roots of the unfolded quiver. For the associated species over finite fields, we realize the polynomials counting absolutely indecomposable representations as graded traces of the unfolding automorphism on preprojective BPS cohomology. Galois-orbit formulas and M\"obius inversion then recover the counts at each residue degree. Finally, we prove an all-rank symmetrizable analogue of Kac's constant-term conjecture: the constant term of the polynomial counting all indecomposables, rather than only absolutely indecomposable ones, equals the corresponding Kac--Moody root multiplicity. This constant is independent of the symmetrizer and modulation.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Tilting bundles and modifying modules in relative dimension one
item.description: arXiv:2611.07987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For projective morphisms $\pi:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over noetherian complete local rings, with fibres of dimension at most one and $\mathbf{R}\pi_*\mathcal{O}_Y\cong\mathcal{O}_X$, we construct a tilting fan from cones of pretilting bundles. Maximal cones parametrize tilting bundles, and facet adjacency encodes irreducible mutation. Completeness in positive rank is equivalent to finiteness of tilting bundles modulo line-bundle twists. For closed fibres that are split ADE highest-root cycles or their Stein contractions, we identify tilting bundles with chambers of restricted affine Tits cones and determine the fan. Over normal Gorenstein complete local domains, reflexive pushforward takes pretilting bundles on normal projective birational models with fibres of dimension at most one and $\pi^!\mathcal{O}_X\cong\mathcal{O}_Y$ to modifying modules. Pushforwards of canonical tilting bundles recover models as module blowups and detect contractions by additive containment, yielding an Auslander--McKay embedding. The hypersurfaces $R=S[[u,v]]/(uv-f)$, with $S$ a regular complete local ring and $f\in S$ a nonzero nonunit, generalize type $A$ Du Val surfaces and $cA_n$ threefolds to arbitrary dimension. We classify modifying modules by divisor flags and rank-one reflexive twists; flag blowups turn the embedding into an equivalence. If $f$ has $r\ge2$ prime factors counted with multiplicity, reflexive pushforward on any maximal-flag model gives a mutation-preserving surjection from tilting bundles, parametrized by chambers of affine type $\widetilde{A}_{r-1}$, to maximal modifying modules. Its fibres are affine Weyl group orbits determined by repeated factors. All maximal-flag models and maximal modification algebras are derived equivalent. These algebras are noncommutative crepant resolutions exactly when $S/(p)$ is regular for every prime factor $p$ of $f$.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Open Problems on the Null Space and Image Space of the Adjacency Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2611.08244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi proposed two questions concerning the null space and the image space of graphs. Although these problems have been studied in several cases, they have not yet been fully resolved. In this work, we present constructions of graphs that satisfy both the problems.
item.dc:creator: K Kranthi Priya, K C Sivakumar

item.title: A Note on the OpenAI Construction of Counterexamples to the Kaplansky Direct-Finiteness Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.08268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a human-readable exposition of OpenAI's construction of a group algebra in characteristic two that is not directly finite. We then adapt the argument to show that, for every prime $p$, there exists a hyperbolic group $G_p$ such that $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ is not directly finite.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain

item.title: Central simple algebras, Milnor $K$-theory and homogeneous spaces over complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2
item.description: arXiv:2501.01403v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field of dimension $2$. We prove the following statements on the arithmetic of $K$. - The ``period equals index'' property holds for central simple $K$-algebras. - If $K$ has characteristic $0$, for every prime $p$, every class in the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ is represented by a symbol. - Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field $K$. That is, for every semisimple and simply connected $K$-group $G$, the set $H^1(K,G)$ is trivial.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Gille, Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche

item.title: Directed partial orders on the complex number field
item.description: arXiv:2609.20494v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a class of positive cones that make $\mathbb{C}$ into a directed partially ordered ring. The positive cones are defined using integral closures of local rings, associated with a transcendence basis and a chosen real generator. A localization criterion also yields such orders on every transcendental extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. For a fixed coefficient field, we prove that two real generators define the same cone if and only if they differ by an affine map with positive real-algebraic slope and translation algebraic over that field. The nonzero positive elements are closed under inversion.
item.dc:creator: Wenyi Wang, Ruisong Yuan, Yuehui Zhang, Yuhang Zhu

item.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replicating for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$. Each generating operation is recovered as the negative sum of two or three split operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd\to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, these constructions are described by Manin black products: \[ \ABSu(\opd)\cong\antiprelie\bullet\opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong\antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we also introduce the canonical quadratic anti-duplicator and anti-triplicator, together with their combinatorial counterparts defined by labeled planar binary trees. We show that they coincide precisely under a full-support condition. As applications, we obtain anti-dupli-com and anti-dupli-Lie algebras. We also display an example in which the two constructions differ. Furthermore, we establish the Koszul duality relations \[ \widehat{\ADup}(\opd^!) \cong\ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \widehat{\ATrip}(\opd^!) \cong\ATSu(\opd)^!, \] providing an effective description of the canonical quadratic anti-duplicator in terms of the Manin white product. The framework recovers known constructions, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie and anti-pre-Poisson algebras, and produces further examples and Koszul dual pairs.
item.dc:creator: Chengming Bai, Li Guo, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang

item.title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.05187v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Gordienko, Maria Morozova

item.title: Weak representability of actions of non-associative algebras
item.description: arXiv:2306.02812v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the categorical-algebraic condition that internal actions are weakly representable (WRA) in the context of varieties of (non-associative) algebras over a field. Our first aim is to give a complete characterization of action accessible, operadic quadratic varieties of non-associative algebras which satisfy an identity of degree two and to study the representability of actions for them. Here we prove that the varieties of two-step nilpotent (anti-)commutative algebras are weakly action representable, and we explain that the condition (WRA) is closely connected to the existence of a so-called strong amalgam. Our second aim is to work towards the construction, still within the context of algebras over a field, of a weakly representing object $\mathcal{E}(X)$ for the actions on (or split extensions of) an object $X$. We actually obtain a partial algebra $\mathcal{E}(X)$, which we call external weak actor of $X$, together with a monomorphism of functors ${\mathrm{SplExt}(-,X) \rightarrowtail \mathrm{Hom}(U(-),\mathcal{E}(X))}$, which we study in detail in the case of quadratic varieties. Furthermore, the relations between the construction of the universal strict general actor $USGA(X)$ and that of $\mathcal{E}(X)$ are described in detail. We end with some open questions. This version is preceded by a corrigendum. Theorem 2.11 of the published article, which states that the variety of commutative associative algebras is weakly action representable, is false: we exhibit a $16$-dimensional algebra $X$ with zero multiplication for which the functor $\mathrm{SplExt}(-,X)$ admits no weak representation. Hence this variety is action accessible but not weakly action representable. The corrigendum amends the statements affected by this error, corrects Proposition 2.8, whose "if" part needs a strong amalgam, updates the definition of partial algebra, and lists some further minor corrections.
item.dc:creator: Jose Brox, Xabier Garc\'ia-Mart\'inez, Manuel Mancini, Tim Van der Linden, Corentin Vienne
